job_description:
Northstar Health Systems is hiring a Backend AI Engineer to join a small platform team building internal AI-assisted workflow products used by clinical operations staff. The engineer will work with product, data, and security teams to build reliable APIs, integrate machine-learning services, and improve the observability of production systems. This is a hands-on engineering role; it is not a research-only position.

Candidates must have at least three years of professional Python development experience and hands-on experience building production APIs with FastAPI or a comparable Python web framework. Strong SQL skills are required because the role owns several PostgreSQL-backed services. Experience packaging and running services with Docker is required. Candidates should also have experience writing automated tests and working with Git-based code review workflows.

The team runs primarily on AWS. Experience with AWS is preferred, especially ECS, Lambda, CloudWatch, or RDS. Familiarity with LLM APIs, prompt-based systems, or retrieval-augmented generation is useful but not required. The role includes reviewing pull requests, documenting service behavior, and participating in an on-call rotation during business hours.

Northstar offers health coverage, a learning budget, and flexible hybrid work. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider qualified applicants without regard to protected characteristics.
resume_text:
Backend software engineer with four years of professional experience building Python services for healthcare and analytics products. Developed REST APIs with FastAPI, Pydantic, and PostgreSQL and wrote integration tests with pytest. Designed SQL queries and database migrations for production services. Containerized applications with Docker and supported CI pipelines in GitHub Actions. Regularly reviewed pull requests and maintained technical documentation for shared services.

Worked primarily in Azure rather than AWS, including App Service, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, and Application Insights. Built one internal prototype using an LLM API to summarize support tickets, but have not deployed a retrieval-augmented generation system to production.
